title: Epochal pin migration, graceful traffic drain, and rollback safeguard for version rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Recent canary rollouts have exposed brittle behavior when we mix session-level pinning with region/tier routing. Users can be pinned to a canary variant while their region falls back to a different tier, causing cross-variant KV cache misses, higher latency, and confusing A/B signal. Goal: define and implement an epoch-based migration and traffic-drain strategy that: (1) preserves deterministic pin semantics during rollouts, (2) enables fast safe rollback without long-lived stale pins, (3) warms caches proactively for the new variant, and (4) provides observable checkpoints for automatic aborts.
description_more: Success criteria: (a) during staged rollouts we should see <5% additional p90 latency across pinned sessions compared to baseline within 10 minutes of the rollout start, (b) rollback should complete within the configured drain window 95% of the time, (c) no cross-tier variant contamination (sessions pinned to variant A seeing inference from B) in production logs. Constraints: must work with existing routing resolver and session affinity layer; minimal customer-visible config changes; must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments where clocks may drift slightly.
proposed_approach: 1) Epoch token: attach a monotonically increasing epoch to rollout versions. When a rollout starts we increment the epoch and emit a migration event. 2) Deterministic assignment: routing resolver uses (session_id, epoch) to derive deterministic pin assignment; if a session has a preexisting pin with older epoch we classify it as 'draining' and schedule a controlled migration. 3) Drain window (configurable, default 300s): pinned sessions transition off the old variant gradually using a rate limiter (e.g., 2%/min throttle) or on-session-graduation hooks for interactive sessions. 4) Cache warming: before sending production traffic to new variant, run async cold-start warmers using sampled prefixes from the session history; KV cache warmers run on the same hardware tier to pre-populate caches. 5) Read-through verification: for the drain window we route read-only requests preferentially to old variant while writes/continuations go to new variant to prevent KV divergence. 6) Rollback safety: maintain a rollback-epoch map and use SLO gates (error budget burn, model quality eval, latency spikes) to trigger fast rollback where new epoch is immediately marked rollback-pending; we then accelerate drain by increasing migration rate and short-circuiting new pins back to previous variant. 7) Observability and abort heuristics: dashboards and automatic aborts based on 5m p95 deltas, quality regression checks against control prompts, and user-visible rollout status API.
implementation_notes: - Routing resolver changes: add epoch to route key and extend deterministic hash to fold epoch in as MSB; graceful behavior for missing epoch field for older clients. - Orchestrator: emit migration events to sessions-service. - Session-service: implement drain scheduler and per-session state 'epoch_pin' with TTL (default 24h) to avoid infinite stickiness. - KV cache warmer: add a 'preheat' job that can run in low-priority slots; must respect tenant isolation. - Metrics: rollout_epoch, epoch_transition_rate, epoch_drain_remaining, preheat_success_rate, rollback_trigger_reasons.
open_decisions: - Exact default drain window: 300s (proposal) vs 900s (conservative). - Migration throttle: percent-per-minute vs absolute concurrent migrations. - Whether to use read/write split for verification (adds complexity) or rely on canary traffic only. - TTL for epoch_pin: 24h recommended but needs privacy/legal review for some customers in Private deployments.
risks_mitigation: - Risk: cache warming may leak memory on constrained tiers. Mitigation: limit preheat concurrency and use soft eviction. - Risk: inconsistent epoch between services due to clock skew. Mitigation: use vector clock emulation via control-plane sequential counters; tolerate +/-1 epochs and fallback to conservative path. - Risk: rollback triggers oscillations. Mitigation: introduce hysteresis and rate-limited rollbacks with manual override.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for deterministic hash with epoch fold-in. 2) Integration test: two-node cluster simulating region tier failover, assert no cross-variant inference. 3) Canary in staging with synthetic sessions and prefix replay to validate warmers. 4) Load test to measure lambda of p95 impact during migration at scale. 5) Chaos run: force rollback and ensure sessions return to previous variant within configured drain window.
